newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan government force kills 69 rebels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sudan government force kills 69 rebels - paper.

text.p: Sudanese government forces killed 69 rebels when they repulsed an attack on two southern towns, a newspaper said on Sunday.

The rebel Sudanese People's Liberation Army (SPLA) tried to take Ayod and Fanjak in the state of Jonglei "for the forceful recruitment of children," the independent Arabic daily Alwan quoted a government spokesman as saying.
David De Chnad, spokesman of the South Sudan Defence Force (SSDF), said 71 rebels were also wounded in the fighting.
The SSDF is comprised of southern Sudanese rebel factions who signed a peace agreement in April with the government of President Omar Hassan al-Bashir.
Last week, the SPLA said in Eritrea that its troops took Ayod, about 840 km (500 miles) south of Khartoum.
